title: He Opened King Tut's Tomb and Died Within Months
description:
In 1923, the man who paid to open King Tut's tomb was dead within months, and the newspapers called it a curse.
But the man who actually broke into the tomb lived 16 more years. So what really happened? The answer is at the end.

All visuals are original illustrations drawn in code; scenes are illustrative reconstructions, not archival footage. Narration uses an AI voice.

hook: In nineteen twenty-three, the man who paid to open King Tut's tomb... was dead within months. The newspapers had a word for it. A curse. Then the deaths kept piling up. A prince. A radiologist. A secretary. But here's the part almost nobody talks about. The man who actually broke into the tomb lived for more than sixteen years after it. So was there ever a curse? Or was something else going on? Stay to the end, because the real answer is stranger than any curse. And part of it was only discovered in twenty twenty-five.
